name: Paya Lebar
summary: East-central office-and-mall hub around Paya Lebar Quarter / EWL–CCL interchange — newer condo gravity with older estate edges toward Geylang and MacPherson.
body: Paya Lebar is the expat shortlist when the job sits in PLQ / SingPost Centre gravity and you want East-West + Circle Line interchange power without moving to the CBD core. Newer condos and commercial towers define the marketing photos; older HDB and walk-up edges toward Geylang, Eunos, and MacPherson still set real rent bands a short walk away. Expect weekday office crowds, mall F&B density, and quieter patches one estate over. Watch-outs: interchange premium pricing, weekend mall traffic, and assuming every side-street is as polished as the Quarter. Compare with MacPherson for cheaper HDB-led living on the same broad catchment, Tai Seng for industrial-edge CCL value, and Eunos / Guillemard when you want slightly calmer residential texture beside the same EWL spine.
bestFor: car-light households who want mall + MRT stacked
couples trading CBD rents for interchange access
renters who will vet condo vs older-edge blocks carefully
watchOuts: Weekday crowd crush at the mall/MRT seam
Sharp quality drop a few streets off the Quarter
Geylang-edge variance if you stretch too far south
housingMix: Newer condos around the commercial hub; mature HDB / walk-ups on the MacPherson, Eunos, and Geylang edges.
commuteNotes: East-West and Circle Line at Paya Lebar; test office peak and the walk from your block to PLQ in a downpour.
